votes.bill_title: Calling on elected officials and civil society leaders to counter antisemitism and educate the public on the contributions of the Jewish-American community.
votes.plain_language: This resolution calls on elected officials, faith leaders, and civil society leaders to condemn and counter acts of anti-Semitism. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports agreeing to it; a Nay opposes it.

posts.text: Looking forward to delivering for the Commonwealth of Virginia! https://t.co/wwqC7jNJ0o

The men and women who serve our country make a commitment that extends far beyond their years in uniform. And the promises we make to them should last just as long.

This week, I joined the groundbreaking for HomePort Hampton Roads 2, an investment in housing for our Navy sailors. In Congress, I’m also supporting the bipartisan Major Richard Star Act to ensure combat-injured veterans receive the full benefits they’ve earned.

Because honoring service isn’t just about what we say on Veterans Day. It’s about what we’re willing to do every day to stand behind those who have stood up for us.

To all our veterans, thank you for your service. Happy Veterans Day.
The American people gave us a clear mandate and we are going to deliver for workers in the 120th Congress. https://t.co/qDXge8q7DG

Today's inflation report reminds us why voters sent a clear message last week. 

Families are tired of working harder, paying more, and still struggling to get ahead. I look forward to working with our incoming Democratic colleagues to deliver meaningful relief. https://t.co/UHi18mRkCA

This month’s job report tells us what we already know, Trump’s economy isn’t working for them. We’re going to fight for an economy that works for everyone, not just the wealthy few. https://t.co/hdGuffJ5Y8

Honored to have the support of @ProtectOurCare. Together, we can reverse Trump’s health care cuts, lower costs for families, and make sure every American has access to quality, affordable care. No one should have to choose between their health and their paycheck. https://t.co/jkJaex7O7w

The Trump Administration is not above the law.

Americans are paying more for just about everything. Health care, gas, groceries, housing. And what did Republicans prioritize? Tax cuts for the wealthy.
We’re not giving up until health care is affordable and accessible for everyone.
Thank you to @ProtectOurCare for standing with us in the fight to lower health care costs for American families.
#SickOfIt #ProtectOurCare

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
